mechanisms.name: 1.12.0 is older than 1.11.5 in security terms (security fixes in 1.11.5 backport missing from 1.12.0)
mechanisms.claimedClassQuote: Going to 1.12.0 would drop those fixes.
mechanisms.mechanism: 1.11.5 lists "Controller: Several security fixes. (#13070)". The 1.12.0 changelog was cut earlier (newest entries Dec 2024) and has no such entry. 1.11.5 was released after 1.12.0 as a backport, so going to 1.12.0 would drop those fixes. The README support matrix shows 1.12.x as no longer supported.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: No mitigation. The cluster has the admission webhook enabled and is public-facing. Recommendation: target at least 1.12.1 (chart 4.12.1), preferably a supported line, 1.13.x or later, and re-run the review against that target.
citedEvidence: 1.12.0 changelog (newest entries Dec 2024, no such entry)
assumptions: From the author's own knowledge, not from the supplied files: the fixes cover the March 2025 ingress-nginx CVEs, including CVE-2025-1974, and landed in 1.11.5 and 1.12.1. Could not be confirmed from the repo.
missingEvidence: Upstream advisory confirming the CVE coverage
Changelog for 1.13+ (not supplied); 1.13+ has its own breaking changes that were not reviewed
recommendedValidation: Verify the CVE claim against the upstream advisory
Decide the real target version (at least 1.12.1, or preferably 1.13+) and redo the render and diff for it

mechanisms.name: --enable-metrics=false arg removed
mechanisms.mechanism: The arg is removed from the rendered controller args.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: 1.12.0 defaults --enable-metrics to off (#12153). controller.metrics.enabled is false in both chart versions, and nothing in env/ enables it.
citedEvidence: chart values (controller.metrics.enabled false in both versions)
recommendedValidation: not stated

mechanisms.name: allow-snippet-annotations: "false" removed from the ConfigMap (open item)
mechanisms.mechanism: The key disappears from the rendered ConfigMap even though the chart's allowSnippetAnnotations: false is the same in both values files. Either the 1.12.0 chart omits the key when it is false, or the controller default changed. If the controller default is not false, snippets would become allowed. That would be a security-posture change, because anyone able to create Ingresses could use snippets.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Nothing in the repo uses snippets, so there is no functional break today.
citedEvidence: chart values files (allowSnippetAnnotations: false in both)
assumptions: The controller's snippet default is from knowledge or inference, not from the supplied files
missingEvidence: The supplied files don't say whether the chart omits the key or the controller default changed
recommendedValidation: Confirm with the chart template or kubectl get cm on staging

mechanisms.name: runAsGroup: 82 added (controller), 65532 (certgen jobs)
mechanisms.mechanism: runAsGroup added to the security context.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The controller image's www-data is already gid 82, per the 4.12.0 values comment. Rated "Low risk."
recommendedValidation: Verify the pod starts

mechanisms.name: kube-webhook-certgen v1.5.2 -> v1.5.0 (downgrade; open item)
resourcesConsumers: admission webhook cert create and patch jobs
mechanisms.mechanism: The chart pins an older certgen version, so this is a downgrade. It affects the admission webhook cert jobs only. The webhook is enabled, so a failed job would block or break Ingress admission.
missingEvidence: Whether v1.5.2 fixed anything that matters
recommendedValidation: Check whether v1.5.2 fixed anything that matters
Confirm the create and patch jobs still complete under Argo CD hooks

mechanisms.name: strict-validate-path-type now on by default
mechanisms.mechanism: Strict path-type validation could reject Ingress paths. This is the most relevant item because the .well-known path contains a dot.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Both paths use only characters that strict validation allows (letters, ., -, /).
assumptions: The contents of the strict path-type regex are from knowledge or inference, not from the supplied files
missingEvidence: Could not test; the validation regex is not in the supplied upstream files
recommendedValidation: Staging run: admission webhook accepts the docs Ingress and rejects a bad one; controller log has no admission or validation errors

mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The only annotation is nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: "false". It is a valid boolean and low risk.
recommendedValidation: Check that the ssl-redirect: "false" behavior is unchanged: HTTP is not redirected

recommendedValidation: Staging: X-Forwarded-* headers behave the same, with use-forwarded-headers and the externalTrafficPolicy: Local client IP
A request with a body over 8m returns 413
HSTS header is present
GET / and GET /.well-known/security.txt return 200 with the expected content

overall.recommendation: Do not proceed with the 1.12.0 target. No documented breaking change appears to break the environment, but 1.12.0 is a security regression from 1.11.5. Target at least 1.12.1 (chart 4.12.1), preferably 1.13.x or later. Re-run the review, render and diff against that target. Before production: a staging run, live cluster drift checks, rollout and PDB checks, external consumer checks, and a rollback plan (pin back to 4.11.5 in Git). Argo CD auto-sync means merging rolls the change out to prod immediately, with no manual gate.
overall.quote: I do not recommend this specific target. 1.12.0 is a security regression from 1.11.5, and a better target exists
